features: NO DATABASE CHANGES — No migrations. What changes is how you get to an installed database, not what is inside it. Nothing changes for whoever installs from the zip with the setup wizard: tried end to end on an empty database before closing, same steps, same order, same result.

THE WIZARD, WITHOUT THE WIZARD — The wizard's steps (migrations, permissions, first administrator, initial data, name and language, closing) are now four services the wizard calls in place of its inline blocks, and that a new command uses with nobody at the keyboard: `php artisan kondomanager:installa` (alias `km:install`). It reads INSTALL_ADMIN_EMAIL and INSTALL_ADMIN_PASSWORD (name optional; APP_NAME and APP_LOCALE for name and language), waits for the database, installs on an empty one. It checks it has everything before writing anything: without the administrator's data it stops and creates no table at all. Repeatable: on an installed database it does nothing; with an administrator but no lock file (source install, recreated container) it just writes the lock. The administrator is created before the initial data, so the seeder's convenience user is never created; from permissions to settings it is one transaction. The password never shows: not in the output, not in messages, not in an error trace.

A DATABASE THAT ALIGNS WITH THE CODE — `php artisan kondomanager:aggiorna` runs the steps the in-app upgrade runs after deploying a zip (migrations, permissions and roles, municipalities, ATECO, recorded version) for whoever changes code another way: a new Docker image, a git pull. Without it, a permission added in code would stay in code.

THE INSTALLER SWITCH FROM THE ENVIRONMENT — INSTALLER_ENABLED, when present, overrides the literal in config/installer.php (setup wizard, update check, automatic update); when absent, the literal applies and nothing changes. Meant for containers, and for whoever wants to turn automatic updates off with a setting that survives updates: .env is among the preserved files, config/ is not.

A CAP ON THE NUMBER OF BUILDINGS — LIMITE_CONDOMINI: absent, empty or zero = no limit (every standalone installation). With a cap, creating beyond it (demo building included) is refused with a neutral message and nothing half-written. The importer does not apply it: it brings in an archive that already exists.

/UP TELLS THE TRUTH — Answers 200 only if the installation is closed (lock, or an administrator), the database answers and no migration is pending; 503 otherwise. Outside the web group (no session per check); from the internet only the status, details from the machine itself or a private network. Applied migrations with no file left are counted and do not make the installation unhealthy.

THE CANONICAL DOCKER IMAGE — Multi-stage Dockerfile at the root, .dockerignore, docker/production/ (nginx, php-fpm, queue worker and scheduler under supervisor, logs to stdout). Non-interactive first start: waits for the database, installs if empty, aligns if present, caches at runtime, then serves. Safe defaults: production, debug off, cache/sessions/queues on the database, installer off, trusted proxies on private networks; without APP_KEY it stops and says so. Tried locally: first start, restart, recreation without a volume. docker/standard and docker/frankenphp untouched.

MAINTENANCE — Weekly cleanup of expired cache rows in the scheduler. A refund test that went red between 22:00 and 24:00 UTC (tomorrow in UTC against the user's today in Rome) now uses the same calendar as the rule.
